:::{#thm-expected-probability-collision}
#### The expected probability is the collision probability

Let $X$ be a [discrete random variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv),
and let $X'$ be an [independent](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/independence.html#def-indpt) copy of $X$.
Then

$$\E{\P(X)} = \sum_x \P(X=x)^2 = \P(X = X').$$

:::

::: proof

The [expectation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-expectation) of a function of $X$ weights each value of the function by the [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) of $x$.
For the function $\P(x)$, which maps each value $x$ to its probability $\P(X=x)$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\E{\P(X)}
&= \sum_x \P(X=x) \, \P(X=x) \\
&= \sum_x \P(X=x)^2.
\end{aligned}
$$

By the definition of the [collision probability](#def-collision-probability), the last sum is $\P(X = X')$.

:::
